item.title: Yamanashi Nature Guide: Climbing Mt Fuji, Shosenkyo Gorge & the Southern Alps
item.description: Yamanashi is defined by extremes of elevation. The prefecture sits in the Kofu Basin at around 250 metres above sea level, but its borders encompass the summit of Japan — Mt Fuji at 3,776 metres — and the highest peaks of the Southern Alps to the west, including Mt Kitadake at 3,193 metres, the country’s second-tallest mountain. Between these extremes stretches a terrain of granite gorges, lava field forests, volcanic ice caves, and river valleys that together constitute one of Japan’s richest and most varied natural environments.
